surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involves alternating pulses of diethylzinc (DEZn), trimethylaluminum (TMA), and water (H2O) vapor, with N2 purge steps. The ALD cycles for ZnO and Al2O3 are described as follows: DEZn pulse (0.01 s) → N2 purge (5 s) → H2O pulse (0.1 s) → N2 purge (5 s) for ZnO, and TMA pulse (0.03 s) → N2 purge (5 s) → H2O pulse (0.1 s) → N2 purge (5 s) for Al2O3.
evidence: ALD proceeds the chemical reactions only at the surface of the substrate, leading to self-limiting and layer-by-layer growth. ALD offers many benefits such as accurate and facile thickness control, excellent conformality, high uniformity over a large area, good reproducibility, low defect density, and low deposition temperatures. Zn(C2H5)2 (diethylzinc, DEZn, the Zn precursor), Al(CH3)3 (trimethylaluminum, TMA, the Al precursor) and H2O vapor (the oxygen precursor) were alternately pulsed into the reaction chamber by a N2 carrier gas flow. The ALD process consisted of two kinds of cycles, one of which contained the following sequence: DEZn pulse, 0.01 s → N2 purge, 5 s → H2O pulse, 0.1 s → N2 purge, 5 s for the deposition of ZnO (ZnO cycle), and the other contained TMA pulse, 0.03 s → N2 purge, 5 s → H2O pulse, 0.1 s → N2 purge, 5 s for the Al doping (Al2O3 cycle).
